title: RSA (Rivest-Shamir-Adleman)
summary: RSA is a public-key cryptosystem. Key generation: choose two large primes p, q; n = p*q; φ(n) = (p-1)(q-1); choose e (public exponent, typically 65537); d = e^(-1) mod φ(n) (private exponent). Encryption: c = m^e mod n. Decryption: m = c^d mod n. Signature: s = m^d mod n. Verify: m = s^e mod n. Padding: PKCS#1 v1.5 or OAEP (encryption), PSS (signature).

Key generation: choose two large primes p, q; n = p*q; φ(n) = (p-1)(q-1); choose e (public exponent, typically 65537); d = e^(-1) mod φ(n) (private exponent). Encryption: c = m^e mod n. structure.meaning: n = p * q. Product of two large primes.
Typically 65537 (0x10001). Must be coprime to φ(n).
d = e^(-1) mod φ(n) (or mod λ(n) for CRT optimization).
dp = d mod (p-1), dq = d mod (q-1), qinv = q^(-1) mod p. Enables 4x faster decryption.
m = c^d mod n (or CRT: m1 = c^dp mod p, m2 = c^dq mod q, then CRT combine).
Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding: adds randomness and structure to prevent attacks.
Probabilistic Signature Scheme: randomized padding for signatures.

notes: RSA key sizes: 2048 bits (minimum), 3072 bits (recommended), 4096 bits (high security).
RSA is quantum-vulnerable (Shor's algorithm factors n in polynomial time).
RSA encryption is slow (~1000x slower than AES). Used for key exchange and signatures, not bulk encryption.
PKCS#1 v1.5 padding is vulnerable to Bleichenbacher's attack; OAEP is preferred.
RSA is used in TLS (key exchange), SSH, code signing, and JWT (RS256).
